files.raw.json: Verbatim bodies of the three data files the site fetches (table CSV, categories JSON, cost CSV) under table_2026_06_25.csv / categories_2026_06_25.json / cost_2026_06_25.csv, plus dom_leaderboard: the full DOM leaderboard extraction before and after the 'Include finetunes' toggle (headers, every row's cells with html and classList), and the id-map source (the 'Add a model to compare' and 'Add a model to the cost chart' select options, plus the pinned radar-chart chips).
files.table_2026_06_25.csv: Verbatim source: per-model, per-subtask scores (23 subtask columns). Model ids are API ids, not display names. Folded into raw.json, not persisted separately, and NOT expanded into normalized.json.
files.categories_2026_06_25.json: Verbatim source: mapping of the 7 categories to their subtasks. Keys are Reasoning, Coding, Agentic Coding, Mathematics, Data Analysis, Language and 'IF' (the matching DOM column header is 'INSTRUCTION FOLLOWING'). Folded into raw.json.
files.cost_2026_06_25.csv: Verbatim source: per-model, per-subtask cost columns plus nq_* (question counts), out_* (output tokens) and the model-level pricing fields. Folded into raw.json; only the model-level fields are lifted into normalized.json.
files.normalized.json: One record per model per metric: 55 models x 8 metrics = 440 records.

fields_added_vs_20260906: score_delta / score_delta_direction - the site now renders a small '+/-X' badge next to some category scores. Present only where the DOM actually shows one (24 of 440 records this scrape, all on the 3 finetune models' Agentic Coding cell, plus every one of their cells for the cost delta below). Not present at all in the 20260906 scrape's DOM, so this is a new site feature, not a gap in the old scrape.
cost_delta_usd / cost_delta_direction - same 'lb-delta' badge, on the Cost per successful task cell. Also only present on the 3 finetunes this scrape.

finetune_of - the finetune rows' model cell now carries a 'class="ftn" data-tip="Finetune of X (Org)"' span with the base model named directly. This is new: the 20260906 scrape explicitly noted 'the DOM still exposes no per-row finetune CSS class or data attribute'. That is no longer true. This scrape still derives is_finetune structurally from the toggle diff (see FINETUNE FLAG note below) rather than trusting the new class, and then uses the new data-tip text only to fill finetune_of once a row is already known to be a finetune.
notes: Data endpoints discovered via performance resource entries: livebench.ai/table_2026_06_25.csv, categories_2026_06_25.json and cost_2026_06_25.csv, all at ?v=1789053188. Newer cache-buster than the 20260906 scrape's ?v=1788705252; the release date is unchanged.

RELEASE SELECTOR: now lists 11 release buttons (2024-06-24, 2024-07-26, 2024-08-31, 2024-11-25, 2025-04-02, 2025-04-25, 2025-05-30, 2025-11-25, 2025-12-23, 2026-01-08, 2026-06-25), more than were visible in the 20260906 DOM dump. The two labeled entries shown in the release-strip text are still only '2024-06-24 - v1' and '2026-06-25 - latest', and the page still states 'Showing LiveBench-2026-06-25 - the latest release.' No release newer than LiveBench-2026-06-25 exists as of this scrape; the extra buttons are older intermediate releases that were always selectable but not enumerated in the prior scrape's notes.
52 models are shown by default (up from 51 on 20260906); the 'Include finetunes' toggle adds 3 more (up from 2), for 55 total (up from 53). All 55 are included.

FINETUNE FLAG: derived structurally, per the task's requirement, not by matching the previous scrape's finetune names. The model list was captured with the toggle off (52 rows), the 'Include finetunes' button was clicked, and the list was captured again (55 rows); the set difference is exactly {Smaug Agentic, Smaug Flash, Smaug Mini}. Unlike 20260906, the DOM now ALSO carries an explicit 'class="ftn"' span with a 'data-tip' naming the base model on these same 3 rows and no others, which corroborates the structural diff independently: 'Smaug Agentic' = 'Finetune of Kimi K3 (Moonshot AI)', 'Smaug Flash' = 'Finetune of DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 (DeepSeek)', 'Smaug Mini' = 'Finetune of Qwen3.8-27B (Alibaba)'.

CSV vs DOM MODEL COUNT MISMATCH: both the table CSV and the cost CSV contain 57 model ids, while the leaderboard renders 55 rows even with finetunes enabled. The two CSV-only ids are again 'deepseek-v4-flash' and 'deepseek-v4-pro' (same two as 20260906). They have no rendered row and therefore no site-aggregated category scores, so they were NOT invented into normalized.json. Their raw subtask rows are preserved verbatim in raw.json's table/cost CSV bodies.

Model id to display name mapping: 53 of 55 pairs were read directly off the site's own radar-chart 'Add a model to compare' select element (option value = API id, option text = 'Display Name · score'). The 2 remaining names are the two models pinned by default in that same radar chart ('Claude Fable 5.1 Max Effort', 'Claude Fable 5 Max Effort'), which are absent from the select's own option list because they are already added. Both were resolved by cross-checking DOM cost against cost_per_successful_task in the cost CSV among the still-unmapped CSV ids: 'Claude Fable 5.1 Max Effort' -> claude-fable-5-1-max-effort (DOM $1.212 vs CSV $1.2117, 0.02% relative difference), 'Claude Fable 5 Max Effort' -> claude-fable-5-max-effort (DOM $1.439 vs CSV $1.4777, 2.69% relative difference, the same rounding gap and the same worst-case model the 20260906 scrape reported for this exact pair).

cost_usd is the site's model-level 'COST PER SUCCESSFUL TASK' in USD, taken from the DOM as in previous scrapes (the base number only, stripped of the new lb-delta badge described above). It is not per-category; it is repeated on every record of a model. The CSV-sourced cost_per_question_usd is a different, lower number (cost per question attempted) and is not a substitute for it.
'Show org' was enabled to obtain the provider column, same as 20260906.

open_weights is read from the 'class="opn"' badge span inside the model name cell (the DOM markup changed slightly since 20260906: the badge is now its own span rather than being inferred from a plain 'open' text node, though the visible effect - an 'open' tag next to the model name - is the same). 19 models are open-weights this scrape, up from 17; the two new ones are 'DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Max Effort' and the new finetune 'Smaug Flash'.
date is the LiveBench release date the scores belong to (2026-06-25), not a model release date.
context_window is not published by LiveBench and is omitted.
Per-subtask scores and per-subtask costs are preserved verbatim in the raw CSVs inside raw.json and are deliberately not expanded into normalized.json, per the task instructions.

DISPLAY-NAME PUNCTUATION DRIFT (not an add/remove): the two 20260906 finetunes 'Smaug-Agentic' and 'Smaug-Mini' (hyphenated) now render as 'Smaug Agentic' and 'Smaug Mini' (space-separated). Their model_id is unchanged ('smaug-agentic', 'smaug-mini') and every one of their score/cost fields is unchanged, so this is joined and treated as the same model, not as a removal plus an addition. Matched by model_id, per the task's instruction not to rely on display-name matching.

NEW SITE FEATURE - score/cost delta badges: exactly the 3 finetune models (Smaug Agentic, Smaug Flash, Smaug Mini) carry a 'lb-delta up|dn' badge on their Agentic Coding score and on their cost. No other model or metric shows one. The badge's up/dn class does not track arithmetic sign consistently across score vs. cost (e.g. Smaug Agentic's cost badge is 'up' next to a NEGATIVE delta of -0.019, while its Agentic Coding badge is 'up' next to a POSITIVE delta of +2.5): it reads as a good/bad color cue (cheaper-is-good, higher-score-is-good) rather than a sign indicator. The site publishes no legend for this, so both the raw delta number and the raw up/dn class are preserved verbatim in normalized.json (score_delta_direction / cost_delta_direction) without reinterpreting them as +/-.

Spot-check rows for this scrape, Coding / Agentic Coding: Grok 4.6 76.8 / 57.0; GPT-6 Astra Max Effort 80.4 / 57.3; Gemini 3.8 Flash High 72.5 / 54.2; GLM-5.3 Flash 79.0 / 56.8; Claude 5 Opus Thinking Max Effort 81.4 / 65.2; Claude Fable 5.1 Max Effort 86.4 / 66.1 - identical to the 20260906 figures for every one of these six models, consistent with the 'zero score changes' finding below. The site lists no variant of these names without an effort or tier suffix: there is no bare 'GPT-6 Astra', 'Gemini 3.8 Flash', 'Claude Opus 5' or 'Muse Spark 1.3' row, and the rows named here (plus 'Muse Spark 1.3 xHigh Effort') are the only ones matching those model families.
changes_vs_20260906: Model count grew from 53 to 55 and record count from 424 to 440. Two models were added and none were removed: 'DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Max Effort' (DeepSeek, open-weights, Overall 81.1, entering at rank 5) and 'Smaug Flash' (Abacus.AI, open-weights, the third finetune alongside Smaug Agentic and Smaug Mini, Overall 77.4, finetune of DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731). Open-weights models grew from 17 to 19 and the finetune roster from 2 to 3. Two 20260906 finetune display names changed punctuation only (Smaug-Agentic -> Smaug Agentic, Smaug-Mini -> Smaug Mini) while keeping the same model_id and identical scores/cost, so they are joined as the same models rather than counted as churn. Every one of the 424 model+metric pairs shared with 20260906 is identical in both score and cost_usd: zero score changes and zero cost changes, so the underlying numbers of this release still have not moved since 20260904, only the roster grew again. The release string is unchanged at LiveBench-2026-06-25 and the release selector still offers no newer option (only the endpoint cache-buster advanced, from ?v=1788705252 to ?v=1789053188); the selector was also found to list 11 release buttons total (back to 2024-06-24), more than the 20260906 notes described, though the two the page highlights as labeled options - v1 and latest - are unchanged. Schema drift: this scrape adds score_delta, score_delta_direction, cost_delta_usd, cost_delta_direction and finetune_of, all newly rendered by the site itself (a 'lb-delta' badge on some cells, and a 'class="ftn" data-tip=...' span naming the base model on finetune rows) and absent from the 20260906 DOM. The delta badges appear only on the 3 finetune models' Agentic Coding and cost cells this scrape; finetune_of is populated for all 3 finetunes.
